note: Model emission: enums, unions, collections, nullability and serialization attributes.

assertions.claim: Most request/response data are immutable `record`s built with object-initializers - nothing is settable after construction.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § opening paragraph; dotnet-calling-endpoints § request bodies

assertions.claim: Request bodies are immutable `record`s built with object-initializer syntax (no builders) - so no model is a positional record.
assertions.defends: dotnet-calling-endpoints § request bodies

assertions.claim: JSON wire names are not the C# property names: every generated model property carries an explicit [JsonPropertyName], which is why asserting on "expected_field" is the right test assertion.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § description (wire names vs C# names); dotnet-testing § asserting on the sent body

assertions.claim: List/array properties are `IReadOnlyList<T>?`; maps are `IReadOnlyDictionary<TKey, TValue>?` - never a mutable collection type and never an array.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Collections

assertions.claim: `required` members must be set - required schema members are emitted with the C# `required` modifier.
assertions.defends: dotnet-calling-endpoints § request bodies

assertions.claim: Only OPTIONAL properties with no default carry [JsonIgnore(Condition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull)] - a required member never does, so it is always serialized.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models/reference.md § Notes (JsonIgnore)

assertions.claim: Models declare their properties explicitly; where a model has no additional-properties map - the common case - unknown fields are dropped on deserialization.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Unknown / future fields

assertions.claim: Their emitted `Core/` carries no additional-properties type at all - that file exists only in a newer generator template.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models/reference.md § Unknown fields; the core-surface CAUTION stamp

assertions.claim: Where you want a client-side guard, opt in explicitly with Validator.ValidateObject(body, new ValidationContext(body), validateAllProperties: true) - which only works because every validation attribute the generator ships derives from ValidationAttribute.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Validation attributes are documentation, not enforcement (the opt-in snippet)

assertions.claim: For your own formatting use the BCL, never the SDK's internal converters - the four date converters are internal, so caller code cannot reference them.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Dates & numbers, second bullet

assertions.claim: Enums are type-safe string-enums (`StringEnum<T>`) or int-enums (`IntEnum<T>`) - both bases exist, over TypedEnum<string,T> and TypedEnum<int,T> respectively.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Enums, first sentence

assertions.claim: Reading back: `.Value` (or the implicit conversion) yields the raw wire value.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Enums, Reading back

assertions.claim: `.Value` is literally what goes on the wire - the generated converter writes it verbatim, which is why an unknown value is serialized verbatim.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Enums, the case-insensitivity paragraph

assertions.claim: Guard unknown values with `instance.IsKnownValue()`.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Enums, Guard unknown values

assertions.claim: Guard unknown values with `TryGetKnownValue(...)` - whose out parameter is `TEnum?`, so `out var known` binds to a nullable at the call site.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Enums, Guard unknown values and the four-line usage snippet

assertions.claim: `FromValue("captured")` returns the `CAPTURED` constant itself - same instance, `IsKnownValue()` true - and the declared casing is what goes on the wire.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Enums, the case-insensitivity paragraph

assertions.claim: `var all = {EnumType}.GetKnownValues();` returns `IReadOnlyCollection<{EnumType}>`.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models/reference.md § enum member discovery

assertions.claim: Use the static constants - each known value is exposed as a public static readonly field of the enum type, holding the wire value.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Enums, use the static constants

assertions.claim: Use the static constants - and they are FIELDS: the known-value table is built by reflecting over public static fields, so a constant emitted as a property would silently vanish from it, taking IsKnownValue() and GetKnownValues() with it.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Enums, use the static constants / Guard unknown values

assertions.claim: A generated enum is declared `[JsonConverter(typeof(StringEnumConverter<{EnumType}>))] public sealed record {EnumType} : StringEnum<{EnumType}>` (the int enum the same over IntEnumConverter/IntEnum).
assertions.defends: dotnet-models/reference.md § full string- and int-enum declarations

assertions.claim: `FromValue` is emitted per enum, not guaranteed on all of them - the schema enums under Models/Enums are the ones that do have it, so `FromValue(...)` is available there for a value not known at compile time.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Enums, the FromValue warning

assertions.claim: Some generated enums - server / environment selectors are the ones to watch - expose only their static constants and keep the conversion helper `protected`, so `{EnumType}.FromValue(someString)` does not compile.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Enums, the FromValue warning

assertions.claim: Path/template params are not type-checked against the route (internally the value is `object?`).
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § base URL / path params

assertions.claim: An enum contributes its wire value and not its C# member name - because a parameter value is normalised by round-tripping it through the JSON serializer, so the enum's converter runs rather than its record ToString().
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § base URL / path params

assertions.claim: APIMatic generates a union `record` under `{RootNamespace}.Models.OneOf` or `.Models.AnyOf`.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Polymorphic union types, first sentence

assertions.claim: A union has no object-initializer - no settable or init member and no accessible constructor, so it can only be built through the generated static factory methods.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Polymorphic union types

assertions.claim: JSON (de)serialization of a union is automatic - the union record carries a generated [JsonConverter], so no caller wiring is needed.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Polymorphic union types

assertions.claim: A payload matching no variant throws: both converters end in `throw new JsonException("JSON does not match … schemas: …")`.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Polymorphic union types, the ⚠ warning

assertions.claim: Unions use the per-variant factories and `TryGet…` readers; `FromValue` belongs to enums.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § the union naming table, closing parenthetical

assertions.claim: `OneOf` - the value is exactly one variant, selected on the wire by a discriminator property; the generated converter reads that property and switches on it.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Polymorphic union types, OneOf bullet

assertions.claim: `AnyOf` - no discriminator.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Polymorphic union types, AnyOf bullet

assertions.claim: `AnyOf` - the converter tries each variant's schema in declaration order and takes the first that deserializes.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Polymorphic union types, AnyOf bullet

assertions.claim: A `OneOf`'s variants are always model or enum references - a `OneOf` has no primitive, list or map variant at all.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Construct, the bolded OneOf sentence

assertions.claim: Every variant a `OneOf` does have gets an implicit conversion to the union.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Construct, the bolded OneOf sentence

assertions.claim: A model `{Variant}` yields the factory `.{Variant}({Variant})`.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § the union naming table, first row

assertions.claim: A model `{Variant}` yields the reader `TryGet{Variant}(out {Variant})`.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § the union naming table, first row
